lesson.title: Saturday Point #4: The Pusher
lesson.hook: Your serve at 30–15 against someone who gets everything back. Five of your lessons, one point. Two choices each shot: the tempting one, and the one that wins.
lesson.memHTML: Pay no bills. Then bring them forward.
lesson.tomorrow: Next time you play a pusher, don't try to out-hit them. Stay in the rally, then use the drop to bring them in.

steps.name: They shade wide
steps.sit: 30–15. The returner has shaded wide to cover your wide serve.
steps.q: Where does your first serve go?
steps.payoff: Away from the lean, they can only block it.
steps.why: They're already standing where the wide serve goes, so they're in time. The T is the long way round from there, and all they can do is block it.

lines.A: Into their lean: they're in time, and it comes back deep.
lines.B: Right: it rushes them. A block, wide to your backhand.

steps.name: Wide to your backhand
steps.sit: Their block lands wide in your backhand corner.
steps.payoff: From this far over, running around leaves a bill you can't pay.
steps.principle: Running around costs a recovery. This ball doesn't pay it back.
steps.why: The ball is already wide. Running around puts you further over, and a pusher gets it back into the corner you left, so you only just reach it. The backhand keeps you closer for their next ball. It's close: the forehand lands more often, so both are fine here.
steps.take: Wide to your backhand? Hit the backhand.

lines.A: Right: it keeps you close enough to cover their next ball.
lines.B: Also fine: you only just reach their angle, but the forehand lands every time.

steps.name: Their angled ball
steps.sit: They angle it into your forehand corner. You reach it outside the sideline.
steps.q: From out here, what do you hit?
steps.payoff: High and deep buys the time to get back.
steps.principle: When you're off the court, the next job is getting back.
steps.why: From outside the sideline the flat line is a low-margin ball, and a pusher still gets it back into your empty court. High and deep gives you the time to recover.
steps.take: Pulled wide? High and deep, then get back.

lines.A: Right: you're back in time, and they can only loop it back.
lines.B: They run it down. You're only just in time, with 63 cm over the net.

steps.name: They're still getting back
steps.sit: Their loop lands short. You step in, and they're still getting back from the corner.
steps.payoff: Down the line goes away from them. At full stretch, all they can do is float it back deep.
steps.principle: Change direction when they're still on their way back.
steps.why: They're still recovering from the corner, so crosscourt goes straight back to them and they rally. Down the line is 4.1 m/s away for them: they can only float it back, and you're set early. It lands 9 in 10 either way.
steps.take: They're still getting back? Down the line.

lines.A: Straight back to them. Back in the rally.
lines.B: Right: away from them. They can only float it back.

steps.name: They wait deep
steps.sit: They float it back and wait two metres behind their baseline.
steps.q: How do you change the game?
steps.payoff: From that deep, the drop makes them sprint, and all they can do is pop it up.
steps.principle: Pushers are comfortable at the back. Bring them forward.
steps.why: A pusher waits deep for the next ball. Harder to the corner just comes back. The drop, as slow as it can be (40 km/h), makes them run 5.1 m/s: they reach it at full stretch and can only pop it up, and you pass the side they left.

lines.A: Right: they reach it at full stretch and pop it up. You pass the side they left.
lines.B: Harder to the corner: they get it back.
